title: SAP Technologies Overview
description: Covers the core SAP components like HANA XS/XSA, BusinessObjects (BOE), Enterprise Portal, and SAP GUI for HTML. This guide outlines their purpose, authentication mechanisms, backends, and how users are managed across systems.

Components.Purpose: Lightweight web application server built into SAP HANA. XS is the classic version, XSA is the modernized runtime based on Cloud Foundry.
Components.Authentication: Supports user/password (native or LDAP), SAML, OAuth for XSA.
Components.User Scope: Users are local to the HANA system unless federated via LDAP or SAML.
Notes: XSA provides isolated tenants (spaces), so user roles are scoped per application.
XS classic used technical users often with high privileges.

Components.Purpose: Reporting, dashboarding, and analytics platform with browser and rich-client interfaces.
Components.Authentication: Supports internal BO users, LDAP, AD, SAP (via SAP Authentication plugin).
Components.Backend: CMS Database (BOE internal), connects to various sources like SAP BW, HANA, SQL.
Components.User Scope: Users are local unless external authentication (e.g., AD/SAP) is configured.
Notes: Integration with SAP systems requires a trust setup or SAP credentials mapping.
Passwords for local BO users often weak or reused.

Components.Purpose: Web-based entry point to SAP services — applications, dashboards, and workflows.
Components.Authentication: JAAS-based login modules; supports user/password, SSO, SAML, SAP Logon Tickets.
Components.Backend: SAP Java stack with User Management Engine (UME), often connected to ABAP or LDAP.
Components.User Scope: Depends on UME source. Users may come from Java DB, ABAP backend, or LDAP.
Notes: Often integrated with ABAP for authentication delegation.
Poorly configured SSO is a common vulnerability.

Components.Purpose: Web version of the traditional SAP GUI, enabling transaction execution via browser.
Components.Authentication: ABAP user authentication: username/password, SSO (SAP Logon Ticket, SAML, X.509).
Components.User Scope: Fully ABAP-based. User management is client-specific.
Notes: SAP* and DDIC users exist in each client.
Users are tightly scoped — same username in client 000 ≠ client 001.

NetWeaver Role.Definition: SAP NetWeaver is the technical foundation for many SAP products.
NetWeaver Role.Purpose: Provides core services like identity management, messaging, and integration (e.g., PI, PO).
NetWeaver Role.Dual Stack: NetWeaver can run ABAP stack, Java stack, or dual-stack (both).
NetWeaver Role.Integration: Connects SAP components (like BOE, Portal, HANA) and external systems.
Notes: NetWeaver ABAP is used for backend logic, Fiori, WebGUI.
NetWeaver Java is often used for Portal, Identity Federation, and Web Services.
